items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a great accomplishment
Such great accomplishment can belong to a practitioner
Possessing this accomplishment makes one dear to the yoginīs
items.inference: A practitioner endowed with the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One who possesses the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation may become dear to the yoginīs.

items.question: Which chapter emerges in the context of Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A chapter is identified by its ordinal position
This chapter is said to have emerged in Candra-dvīpa
The ordinal position specified is the ninth
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this meditative posture?
premises: The self is to be contemplated as surrounded by fire
The self is to be contemplated as standing on one foot
These attributes define a specific meditative visualization
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What revelation about knowledge is requested from the deity?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly
The speaker requests a determination of knowledge
The request is for this determination to be made manifest now
items.inference: The deity is asked to make manifest the determination of knowledge to the speaker.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What structural division of teachings is sought to be fully known?
premises: There exists a division of eight octads
The speaker seeks to know this division fully
The knowing is desired in an endless or complete manner
items.inference: The speaker seeks to fully and endlessly know the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: And to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How can the wheel be quickly accomplished in the secret place?
premises: There is a secret place relevant to practice
The wheel is the object to be accomplished
The accomplishment can occur quickly under certain conditions
items.inference: The question seeks the means by which the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel is quickly accomplished in the secret place.

items.question: Why does the deity praise the goddess for her difficult question?
premises: The deity expresses strong approval to the great goddess
The deity has been asked a question
The matter asked about is hard to obtain even for the gods
items.inference: The deity praises the goddess because she has asked about something rare and difficult even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess! I have been asked about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
These assignments map syllables to bodily locations
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is located at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form but may indicate the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is at the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
These assignments continue the mapping of syllables to locations
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is located in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What teaching follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
A meditation related to these wheels remains to be taught
The listener is instructed to hear this meditation
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: What is the form of the divine lotus associated with the first octad?
premises: The lotus is divine and has eight spokes
The lotus is adorned by the first octad
These features define its meditative form
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: A divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an equal mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal or balanced mind
Village duties represent conventional obligations
A practitioner with such a mind should abandon those duties
items.inference: Through practice, one whose mind has become equal should abandon village duties.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to conventional social duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an equal mind, one should abandon the duties of village life.

items.question: What powers arise from the practice associated with this stage?
premises: Knowledge of hearing distant things can arise
Paralysis of bonds can likewise arise
These are presented as attainments to the beloved
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the paralysis of bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or paralyzing bonds
items.plain_english: Knowledge of hearing from afar, and likewise the paralysis of bonds, O beloved.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly summarized at this stage?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as another attainment
These are stated briefly to the goddess
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may mean transformation or reversal
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, immortality and transformation, in brief.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized in meditation?
premises: The second wheel has eight petals
It is associated with meditation on fire or radiance
This meditation makes it well illuminated
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is eight-petaled, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The practitioner’s mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation
Such absorption enables creative power
The practitioner can produce form in many ways
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create forms in many ways.

items.question: What destructive power can an angered adept exercise over the triple world?
premises: The adept can become angry in this state
The triple world includes moving and unmoving beings
The adept has the power to destroy all of it
items.inference: When angered, the adept can destroy the entire triple world with all its moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: The third wheel is described as great
There are nine principles relevant to bondage
This wheel functions as a liberator from those nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates one from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this wheel’s practice?
premises: The practice can destroy wrinkles and grey hair
The practice can grant seeing from very far away
These are presented as parallel attainments
items.inference: This practice brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power of seeing from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a devoted practitioner cultivate multiple forms in solitude?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude
The practitioner should be intent on meditation
The practitioner is instructed to create forms in many ways
items.inference: In solitude, being intent on meditation, the practitioner should create forms in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create forms in many ways.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice
Constant practice produces a transformative result
That result is immortality
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect death from aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is practiced
Death associated with aging is a threat
This practice leads to overcoming that death
items.inference: Through non-eating by day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ may idiomatically mean will go beyond or overcome death
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The practitioner engages in constant yogic practice
The duration implied is sixteen years
This practice results in a specific bodily form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ interpreted as the form of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from constantly contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: The practitioner should constantly contemplate a smoke-colored form
Such contemplation produces a powerful effect
The effect extends to the triple world
items.inference: By constantly contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: Always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world, O beloved.
